name: 74HC590ADWR
title: SN54HC590A, SN74HC590A: 8-bit binary counter with 3-state output register
summary: An 8-bit binary up-counter whose count is copied into an 8-bit register on a separate clock; the register drives eight 3-state outputs. The counter has an asynchronous active-low clear, an active-low count enable and an active-low ripple-carry output for chaining. It runs from 2 V to 6 V. 74HC590ADWR is the SN74HC590ADWR: wide SOIC-16 (DW), -40 °C to 85 °C, reel of 2000.

pins.name: RCO
pins.function: Ripple-carry output, active low. Goes low while the counter stands at hex FF; used to cascade counters.

pins.name: CCLR
pins.function: Counter clear, active low. A low resets the 8-bit counter to zero at once, with no clock needed.

pins.name: CCLK
pins.function: Counter clock. The counter steps up by one on each rising edge while CCKEN is low.

pins.name: CCKEN
pins.function: Counter clock enable, active low. Low lets CCLK edges advance the counter; high holds the count.

pins.name: RCLK
pins.function: Register clock. A rising edge copies the counter's present value into the 8-bit storage register.

pins.name: OE
pins.function: Output enable, active low. Low drives QA to QH from the register; high puts them in the high-impedance state.

circuits.title: Load circuit for switching measurements
circuits.description: The output under test sees CL to ground at the test point, and RL from the test point to a node that S1 can pull to VCC and S2 can pull to ground. Both switches stay open for propagation delay and transition time; for enable and disable times one of them closes, as the load circuit settings table lists.
notes: CL is 50 pF or 150 pF to match the switching table in use; disable times are measured with 50 pF.

operation.text: Inside are an 8-bit binary up-counter and an 8-bit storage register fed from it. The register drives eight 3-state outputs, QA to QH. Counter and register each have a clock of their own.

CCLK advances the counter on its rising edge while CCKEN is held low; with CCKEN high the count stays put. A change on CCKEN by itself never clocks the counter. CCLR low clears the counter to zero asynchronously.
A rising edge on RCLK loads the present count into the register. OE low puts the register contents on QA to QH; OE high floats them. Switching OE does not disturb the counter or the register.

CCLK and RCLK may be wired together. The register then always holds the value one count behind the counter. Run separately, RCLK must rise at least tsu after CCLK for the register to capture a settled count.
RCO goes low while the counter holds hex FF. Two counters chain by taking RCO of the first to CCKEN of the second. For longer chains, RCO of each counter feeds the CCLK input of the next one.

The timing diagram runs through: an asynchronous clear; one count to 01 while the register takes 00; a register load of 01 with CCKEN high so the count stops; counts 02 and 03; outputs at high impedance during the count to 04, then driven again; the count reaches 05 and the register takes 05; the counter runs on through FD, FE and FF, where RCO is low, and wraps to 00, which the register then takes.
Register outputs are rated for ±6 mA at 5 V and up to 15 LSTTL loads. Typical tpd is 14 ns. Input current is at most 1 µA and ICC at most 80 µA (SN74HC590A).
Unused inputs must be tied to VCC or GND. At VCC = 2 V, an input that lingers between 0.5 V and 1.5 V can be flipped by ground noise and double-clock the part.

SN74HC590A parts are rated -40 °C to 85 °C in PDIP (N), SOIC (D) and wide SOIC (DW). SN54HC590A parts are rated -55 °C to 125 °C in CDIP (J), CFP (W) and LCCC (FK). A QML military version of the SN54HC590A exists.
